units.source_en: On the front of the castle and on each of the four sides of its frame it bore the inscription “Castle of Caution.”

Four skillful tabor and flute players accompanied them, and the dance having been opened, Cupid, after executing two figures, raised his eyes and bent his bow against a damsel who stood between the turrets of the castle, and thus addressed her:

paragraphs.source_en: I am the mighty God whose sway Is potent over land and sea. The heavens above us own me; nay, The shades below acknowledge me. I know not fear, I have my will, Whate’er my whim or fancy be; For me there’s no impossible, I order, bind, forbid, set free.

units.source_en: I am the mighty God whose sway Is potent over land and sea.
The heavens above us own me; nay, The shades below acknowledge me.
I know not fear, I have my will, Whate’er my whim or fancy be; For me there’s no impossible, I order, bind, forbid, set free.

paragraphs.source_en: Having concluded the stanza he discharged an arrow at the top of the castle, and went back to his place. Interest then came forward and went through two more figures, and as soon as the tabors ceased, he said:

units.source_en: Having concluded the stanza he discharged an arrow at the top of the castle, and went back to his place.
Interest then came forward and went through two more figures, and as soon as the tabors ceased, he said:

paragraphs.source_en: But mightier than Love am I, Though Love it be that leads me on, Than mine no lineage is more high, Or older, underneath the sun. To use me rightly few know how, To act without me fewer still, For I am Interest, and I vow For evermore to do thy will.

units.source_en: But mightier than Love am I, Though Love it be that leads me on, Than mine no lineage is more high, Or older, underneath the sun.

paragraphs.source_en: Interest retired, and Poetry came forward, and when she had gone through her figures like the others, fixing her eyes on the damsel of the castle, she said:

units.source_en: Interest retired, and Poetry came forward, and when she had gone through her figures like the others, fixing her eyes on the damsel of the castle, she said:

paragraphs.source_en: With many a fanciful conceit, Fair Lady, winsome Poesy Her soul, an offering at thy feet, Presents in sonnets unto thee. If thou my homage wilt not scorn, Thy fortune, watched by envious eyes, On wings of poesy upborne Shall be exalted to the skies.

paragraphs.source_en: Poetry withdrew, and on the side of Interest Liberality advanced, and after having gone through her figures, said:

units.source_en: Poetry withdrew, and on the side of Interest Liberality advanced, and after having gone through her figures, said:

paragraphs.source_en: To give, while shunning each extreme, The sparing hand, the over-free, Therein consists, so wise men deem, The virtue Liberality. But thee, fair lady, to enrich, Myself a prodigal I’ll prove, A vice not wholly shameful, which May find its fair excuse in love.
